title: A jealous theater leader and the move to the Chauffeur's Club
summary: The theater leader Cranshaw resented his piano and demanded he buy a new horn, so Randolph took Shirley Clay's higher-paying job at the Chauffeur's Club.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well, before you leave St. Louis, you were going to mention something about the Chauffeur's Club.

Oh, well, now. Now, here's the way this happened, the show at the Club. My (unintelligible) gave me the job, because he's going to Chauffeur's Club. Shirley Clay was going to Chauffeur's Club, so he had me to take the job at the theater. All right. So, finally, after I stayed there for awhile, Shirley came to me again and asked me if I wanted a job, if I wanted to come to Chauffeur's. He was going to New York.

I told him yes. I wanted it -- and I really wanted it because the leader and I wasn't getting along any too well, and this way -- they tried to put this in the paper, like I said it I say, but he missed -- now, I laughed about the piano -- and the

leader at the theater was kind of jealous in a way. He didn't have a piano and when I bought my piano then it made him jealous. Then he wanted me to buy a horn. Well, now, he knew that the theater was paying -- that theater there was paying $25.00. Now, he knew $25.00 a week and paying for a piano and paying for room, paying for my room rent, or whatever it was, me and my wife, where was staying, and to have to , you know, pay upkeep of the wife and things like that -- why, he figured that something got to give.
You couldn't afford a new horn.

Couldn't afford a new horn. But, yeah, see. So, when he told me I had to have a new horn, see, the boss was kicking on me. I went to the boss -- I'm thinking that the boss is kicking, I said -- and I switched it around turned the thing around when I went to the boss, see. I said, "Louie, I want to see you just a minute." Louie came to me and said, "Yes, what do you want?" I said, "My horn is playing me kind of bad and," I says, "what I'd like to do," I said, "I'd like for you to buy me a new horn and take it out -- take out a few dollars each week until I pay for it." He says, "Your horn playing you bad?" He says, "I don't see nothing about your horn playing bad. It sounds all right to me." I said, "Do you like the way it sounds?" He said, "Yes, I like the way it sounds." He say, "Yeah, I said, "Okay, all right (Unintelligible)" "Save the money," he told me, "Save the money." I said, "Okay." So, then I knew
Yeah, well, I played a trumpet.
You were playing a trumpet back then?
Yeah, I had the trumpet then. But I didn't let on one thing. I didn't go back and tell the leader one thing, you see.

[Cranshaw] I heard he was passed on now. So, then, when Shirley Clay came and told me he was going to New York and asked me would I take this job, why, then, you know I wanted to get away from [Cranshaw]. I told him yes. Then the job was paying $10.00 more. See, I was getting $25.00 at the theater and there I was getting $35.00 at Chauffer's Club. So, I went to Chauffer's Club.
